structured_output.what_is_happening: A pump.fun token named "Spider-Man" graduated to PumpSwap and ran about 12x in its first ~37 minutes, reaching roughly $630k market cap. Its description is just "A man who dresses in a spider outfit". It has no website, no Telegram and no DexScreener profile. The only X handle linked to it is @SpiderManMovie, which is the official Sony/Marvel movie account and is not tied to the token. I found no fresh catalyst that lines up with the launch time (01:21 UTC Sept 22). The Spider-Man IP itself is very hot: Brand New Day passed The Force Awakens as the #1 domestic grosser around Sept 17-18. But that news is several days old and does not point to this contract. The trading looks automated. There were about 20.8k transactions for about $147k of volume, an average trade of about $7. Unique buyers (3,032) and unique sellers (3,007) are nearly equal. The pattern fits volume or bundle bots better than organic buyers. Price was already -45% over 30 minutes and -22% over 1 hour when the data was collected, with only a short +21% bounce over 5 minutes.

narrative.description: A generic 'Spider-Man' memecoin riding on the franchise's 2026 box-office success (Brand New Day is the #1 domestic grosser of all time). There is no specific meme, viral clip or event tied to this token.
narrative.why_spreading: I found no organic spread. The attention seems to come from pump.fun graduation and trending feeds, likely boosted by small bot trades. The broader Spider-Man hype is real but days old, and nothing points to this particular token.

token_connection.why_this_token: Of at least 10 same-name tokens launched in the past day or so, this is the only one with meaningful liquidity or volume. Its only claim to be the one people mean is that it won pump.fun's graduation lottery. It borrows the official movie X handle and has no community of its own.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 9 other Spider-Man / SPIDERMAN tokens were launched between Sept 20 and 22, all dead ($2-5k market cap, zero hourly volume). Older Spider-Man tokens also exist on Raydium (e.g. Spider², SPIDERMAN CTO).

authenticity.evidence: Searches for the contract address on web and X returned nothing. There is no project site and no socials apart from the borrowed official @SpiderManMovie handle. The trading pattern looks botted: about 20.5k transactions averaging about $7 each, and nearly equal unique buyer and seller counts. Holder concentration looks healthy (top 10 about 15.5%, with the pool probably included), the creator's balance is negligible, and LP is 100% locked.
authenticity.uncertainty: X is poorly indexed, and the X page returned HTTP 402, so pump.fun replies and X chatter may exist that I could not see. Private Telegram groups are invisible to me.

structural_risks: Price was already falling from the post-graduation peak: -45% over 30 minutes and -22% over 1 hour
Probable bot or volume-farming transactions (about $7 average trade) inflate the activity numbers
About $71k liquidity against a $630k market cap, so the pool is thin
Many same-name tokens compete for attention, and copycats can launch at any time
The name uses the Marvel/Sony IP with no link to the rights holders

structured_output.counterargument: Spider-Man is one of the most recognisable IPs in the world, and it is in its biggest cultural moment ever: the #1 domestic grosser, a $2.4B+ worldwide total, and NYCC reveals coming Oct 8-11. This token has clearly won the name among pump.fun copies. Holder distribution is clean (3k+ holders, top 10 about 15%, locked LP, creator holds almost nothing). A generic mega-IP token can sometimes hold a few million in market cap on name recognition alone, and the +21% bounce over 5 minutes could be the start of a second leg.

source_coverage.notes: News coverage found concerns the franchise (the box-office record), not the token. The X profile fetch returned HTTP 402, and the pump.fun page did not show token details. I checked DexScreener and GeckoTerminal through their APIs.

structured_output.thesis: This is a generic IP-name token that won the pump.fun graduation among many Spider-Man clones. It has no specific catalyst, no community of its own and no organic social trace I could find. Activity looks bot-inflated, and price was already down 45% from its 30-minute high. I expect the attention to fade.
